stem: When updating post-transplant vaccination teaching, which inactivated vaccine aligns with standard health-maintenance references for recipients not immunized before transplantation?

options.text: Hepatitis A and B vaccines if not immunized pretransplant
Live varicella vaccine for all recipients immediately after transplant
No hepatitis vaccination is ever recommended after transplantation
Only live herpes zoster vaccine is recommended post-transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Health maintenance after transplantation includes obtaining recommended inactivated vaccinations such as hepatitis A and B if the recipient was not immunized pretransplant, along with annual inactivated influenza and pneumococcal vaccine.

rationale_incorrect.B: Live varicella vaccine is contraindicated after transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hepatitis A and B vaccination is recommended when pretransplant immunization was incomplete.
rationale_incorrect.D: Live herpes zoster vaccine is contraindicated after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Hepatitis A and B if not immunized pretransplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance → ii. (hepatitis A and B if not immunized pretransplant); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Hepatitis A/B post-transplant vaccination angle distinct from household influenza teaching (cctc-1139) and vaccination combo (cctc-1048); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A kidney recipient asks why post-transplant vaccine timing differs from the general population. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Transplant recipients may require vaccine boosters earlier due to immunosuppression
Immunosuppression eliminates the need for any post-transplant vaccinations
Vaccine boosters should always be deferred until ten years after transplant
Immunosuppression makes live-virus vaccines the preferred post-transplant option

explanation.rationale_correct: Health maintenance teaching notes that transplant recipients may require vaccine boosters earlier because immunosuppression can reduce vaccine response, while live-virus vaccines remain contraindicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Inactivated vaccinations remain important after transplantation rather than being eliminated.
rationale_incorrect.C: Earlier boosters may be needed rather than deferring all vaccination for a decade.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppressed patients should not receive live-virus vaccines after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Transplant recipients may require boosters earlier, due to immunosuppression

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

notes: Source-first item. Earlier-booster counseling angle distinct from pneumococcal timing in health-maintenance combo (cctc-1141) and hepatitis A/B recall (cctc-1146); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A transplant recipient reports disappointment that recovery progress is slower than expected and feels increasingly anxious. Which psychological-care teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Differences between perceived expectation and actual outcome may affect psychological health
Psychological distress never occurs after successful transplantation
Expectation mismatch is unrelated to post-transplant mental health
Psychological concerns should never be discussed with the transplant team

explanation.rationale_correct: Psychological care teaching recognizes that differences in perceived expectation versus actual outcome may contribute to the patient's psychological health, along with monitoring for depression and anxiety.

rationale_incorrect.B: Psychological distress including depression and anxiety may occur and warrants monitoring.
rationale_incorrect.C: Expectation-versus-outcome differences are specifically cited as a psychological health factor.
rationale_incorrect.D: Open monitoring and support for psychological concerns are part of post-transplant care.

stem: A coordinator is revising post-transplant health-maintenance and psychological-care teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Hepatitis A and B vaccines should be given if the recipient was not immunized pretransplant.
Transplant recipients may require vaccine boosters earlier due to immunosuppression.
Live-virus vaccines are appropriate routine post-transplant immunization for all recipients.
The patient should be monitored for signs of depression and anxiety.

explanation.rationale_correct: Hepatitis A/B vaccination when indicated, earlier boosters due to immunosuppression, and depression/anxiety monitoring are supported. Statement III is false because immunosuppressed patients should not receive live-virus vaccines.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—psychological monitoring for depression and anxiety is recommended.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because live-virus vaccines are contraindicated after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → f. Psychological care and g. Health maintenance
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Hepatitis A and B if not immunized pretransplant … boosters earlier … should not receive live-virus vaccines … Monitor patient for signs of depression and anxiety

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → f. Psychological care → ii. and g. Health maintenance → ii. (hepatitis A/B, earlier boosters, live-vaccine contraindication, depression/anxiety monitoring); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Health-maintenance/psychological combo distinct from prior health-maintenance combo (cctc-1141) and vaccination combo (cctc-1048); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.
